one_liner: Otter.ai has a REST public API (bearer API keys) available only to Enterprise workspaces via an account manager; an official MCP server is likely but not confirmed by the fetched pages.
auth_notes: The public API uses bearer API keys created under Integrations → Developer (max 2 per user). OAuth2 is listed only because the Composio catalog shows DCR_OAUTH for the Otter MCP. The fetched pages do not confirm this. The tryotter.com Partner Hub pages belong to a different product, the Otter restaurant platform, and were not counted.
access_notes: The public API is for Enterprise workspaces only. If it is not visible, the docs say to contact the Otter account manager. The pages do not mention a 100-user minimum, so that claim was dropped. No free path to API credentials is documented.
blocker_notes: The REST API requires an Enterprise plan and enablement through the account manager. The fetched pages say nothing about the MCP server, so its tool count, read-only status and tier availability are unverified. It was kept as official on the strength of the hint and the Composio catalog entry (otter_ai_mcp, 3 tools). Confidence in that is low.

evidence.quote: All API requests require authentication using Bearer token authentication.
Note**: There is a limit of 2 API keys per user.
This content is available for the **Otter Enterprise** plan and may require admin permissions.
If you do not see this feature for your workspace, contact your Otter account manager.
